calibration.identityNote: No identity stop is declared. Confirmed by exhaustive grep of all three brand-theme sources for a literal `chrome.sidebar.tone` (or `sidebar: { tone: ... }`) assignment: zero matches -- same law as typography.pairing/surfaces.elevation-posture/shape.button-style (F4B-8).

measuredResult.authorityFix: TWO ingress defects, both by keypath, neither by compiler, plus a DT-adjudicated widening. (1) `chrome.sidebar.*` is a wildcard; `ingressPathMembers`/`resolveIngressMember` only understand brace SETS (`{a,b,c}`), so `*` resolved to itself as a literal member, writing to the nonsense key `chrome.sidebar['*']` -- a false-INERT-by-path defect, same class as F4B-13's motion.dial preflight finding on `motion.*`. Fixed to the real field `chrome.sidebar.tone` (SIDEBAR_TONE_FIELD, chrome-variables/index.ts:194), matching `migrateV1` and `chromeToVariables`'s own reads. (2) `--ds-sidebar-item-color` (declaredOutputs) is a DIFFERENT leaf's channel, written unconditionally from `s.itemColor` (chrome-variables/index.ts:1351) and never touched by the tone. (3) DT widening ruling (F4B-12): declaredOutputs was widened from 2 channels to the full closed six-channel `SIDEBAR_TONE_LEAF_FIELDS` table (chrome-variables/index.ts:184-191) -- the control's authority IS that table, and 2-of-6 under-declared the real governed surface. `--ds-sidebar-item-color` (no -active) stays excluded as the wrong neighbour leaf.
measuredResult.staticArm: 18/18 lowerings alive (3 verticals x 3 stops x 2 modes; a lowering counts as alive when at least one of its 6 channels moves) -- measured directly from the artifacts, not assumed. Channel-level union across both modes (9 scenarios x 6 channels = 54 cells): 52/54 moved, byte-identical to sidebarToneToChrome's own expansion (chrome-variables/index.ts:126-174) wherever they moved; the 2 non-movers are named and explained in unmeasuredScope (a value coincidence with the vertical's own authored baseline, not a broken lowering).
measuredResult.dbArm: 18/18 lowerings alive, same definition and same result as the static arm -- `sidebarToneToVariables` (appearance/index.ts:664) calls the SAME `sidebarToneToChrome` the static arm's `chromeToVariables` calls, so both doors share one lowering by construction, not by coincidence. Channel-level union: 52/54 moved, the identical 2 non-movers as the static arm (same scenario, same channel, same value on both doors).
measuredResult.guardH2: assertStopDiscrimination PASS on both arms, all 3 verticals, all 3 stops as witnesses -- no stopDiscriminationException needed. `sidebarToneToChrome` fully populates all 6 channels for every one of the 3 tones (no empty-preset stop, unlike surfaces.elevation-posture's `soft`), so there is no structural non-mover by design.
measuredResult.ingressEquivalence: Byte-exact between static-brand-theme and db-tenant-theme in all 18 comparisons (scenario x mode), the 6 channels each time, non-movers included -- both doors agree on the 2 non-movers too, not just the 52 that moved.
measuredResult.restore: restore.exact = true on all 9 receipted scenarios, zero differing rows.
measuredResult.negativeWitness: All 4 declared negative controls resolved and held on every receipted scenario: control height, font metrics, border, motion (every declared-target/every-measured-target as scoped). Additionally, and OUTSIDE the negativeControls mechanism (no existing vocabulary phrase covers 'one specific colour channel among many stays fixed', and the write-set does not extend negative-controls/vocabulary.json): `--ds-sidebar-item-color` (the neighbouring itemColor leaf, chrome-variables/index.ts:1351, `s.itemColor`) was added to token-readout/tokens' direct-read set and measured DIRECTLY in the raw artifact on all 9 scenarios -- it never moved, proving the tone reaches exactly its own 6 channels and not the leaf next to it (the same leaf the registry's prior, wrong declaredOutputs entry named).
measuredResult.capabilityPropagation: src/tooling/testing/integration/capability-propagation/tests/index.test.ts's 'consumer reachability -- closes the loop for the ledgered capabilities' test is GREEN today: `navigation.sidebar-tone` is present in its `CONSUMER_REACHED` set (line 349) and the suite's own reachability check (moved channel intersects `menu.css`'s source, via `--ds-sidebar-item-color-active` among others) passes. Declared per DT request (F4B-12 widen adjudication, point 6). Attribution caveat, stated honestly: this suite's own MUTATORS entry for the control writes directly to `sidebarTone`/`chrome.sidebar.bg` on a compiler-input document, bypassing this control's registry `staticBrandThemePath`/`declaredOutputs` entirely -- so the pass is not mechanically downstream of this packet's keypath/widening fix. It is more likely explained by this packet's dist rebuild(s) (the same class of staleness F4B-11 diagnosed and fixed), which this suite's `compileDb`/`compileStatic` calls depend on. One unrelated, pre-existing failure was observed in the SAME file (`does not let one capability move another capability's exclusive channel`, about `typography.families` vs `--ds-font-family-heading` -- not `navigation.sidebar-tone`, not touched by this packet's write-set, not investigated further here).

unmeasuredScope: Only the 6 declared channels were bound as the direct-read fixture target (representativeOnly: true, same convention as the other Standard posture controls). `sidebarToneToChrome` writes exactly these 6 and nothing else, so this is not a partial view of a wider expansion.

Light mode: not separately receipted per-mode; `strong` itself branches on mode internally (chrome-variables/index.ts:140-159, different palette for light vs dark) and that branch is exercised by the causal run's own mode composition (M-1), but per-mode divergence was not individually characterised the way surfaces.elevation-posture's was.
Responsive divergence (one viewport, 1280x800 dpr1) was not measured.

All 3 verticals DO author the six tone leaves literally in their own baseline theme (rottay/bithire/evnto's `chrome.sidebar.{bg,text,textMuted,itemBgHover,itemBgActive,itemColorActive}`), so a VALUE coincidence between an authored leaf and a tone stop's expansion (bithire-style non-mover, F4B-9/F4B-10/F4B-11 precedent) was a real possibility, not a hypothetical -- checked directly against the artifacts, not assumed. Measured (union across both arms and both modes, per scenario x channel, 9 x 6 = 54 cells): 52/54 moved, 2 genuine non-movers, both the SAME benign class as bithire/sober in F4B-11 (the stop's recipe resolves to the same computed value the vertical already authors, light mode): `bithire-subtle` / `--ds-sidebar-text` (bithire authors `text: "#14283B"` literally; `subtle`'s `var(--ds-color-text-primary)` resolves to that same `#14283B` for bithire's light mode) and `evnto-subtle` / `--ds-sidebar-bg` (evnto authors `bg: '#fafafa'` literally; `subtle`'s `var(--ds-color-bg-secondary)` resolves to that same `#fafafa` for evnto's light mode). Neither is a broken door: both arms agree on the non-move (ingressEquivalence still holds), and every one of the 18 (scenario x mode) lowerings still shows at least one of the other 5 channels moving -- see measuredResult.staticArm/dbArm. The check compared only the 3 verticals' CURRENT authored values against the 3 stops' expansions, not every possible leaf/stop combination a future theme edit could introduce. This is a value-coincidence risk, distinct from the RANK mechanism (see B-2 drill 6's own fix): a vertical's baseline-authored leaf never enters `tenantAuthoredPaths` regardless of its value, so it can only create a non-mover by numeric coincidence, never by outranking the tone.
calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: `color remains fixed` is deliberately NOT declared -- this control's entire job is moving colour channels (background/text/item colours), so a blanket colour negative control would assert against the very channels the tone legitimately moves. No vocabulary phrase exists for 'one specific colour channel among many stays fixed' (checked negative-controls/vocabulary.json; the write-set does not extend it), so the neighbouring-leaf proof is NOT a formal negativeControls entry -- it is a direct measurement instead: `--ds-sidebar-item-color` (chrome-variables/index.ts:1351, `s.itemColor`, a DIFFERENT leaf, the exact channel the registry's prior declaredOutputs entry mistakenly named) was added to token-readout/tokens and read directly on every scenario; see measuredResult.negativeWitness for the result.
